newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end softer, consolidation seen.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end softer, consolidation seen.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended softer on Wednesday, surrendering earlier gains as the market headed into a consolidation phase, analysts said.
The TSE 300 Composite Index slipped 4.10 points to close at 6428.62 in turnover of 99.17 million shares worth C$1.54 billion ($1.1 billion).
Advancing and declining stocks were even at 485 each, with 309 issues unchanged.
"Stock markets have had a strong run up and there are no major earnings in the near term. I think the market is due for some consolidation," said CIBC Wood Gundy chief strategist Subodh Kumar.
Kumar said the Canadian market would likely trade in a narrow range in the near term.
"There is a preference for companies with more predictable earnings profile, which is also a sign of a more conservative market," he said.
Gold, base metals and communications led losses in seven of 14 sectors. Gains in banking, retail and technology stopped the TSE from falling as far as Wall Street.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped more than 42 points on Wednesday.
* Skyjack Inc. was the top gainer, climbing 4.25 to 24 after posting record fourth-quarter sales but weaker earnings.

* Northern Telecom Ltd. added 2.50 to 119.50 after winning a $130 million contract on Wednesday. Company officials also said they were comfortable with analysts' estimates for higher second-quarter profits.
* BCE Inc., Canada's biggest publicly traded firm, fell 0.15 to 37.85 after earlier hitting a 52-week high of 38.70.

* Among the banks, Toronto-Dominion Bank rose 0.15 to 42.55. Embattled retailer Eaton's said on Wednesday it sold its 20 percent stake in a landmark Toronto shopping mall to a Toronto-Dominion unit and Cadillac Fairview Corp.
